output_text: {"regions":[{"label":"Figure 3.7 — Risks to market structure and market power stemming from platform firms","kind":"diagram","bbox":[0.117,0.613,0.91,0.923],"summary":"Flow diagram showing how data inputs and data-related advantages can reinforce platform market power, concentration, and conglomeration, with effects varying by platform business model.","details":"The diagram begins with “Data as an input into economic activity,” associated with potential platform sides: consumers; suppliers or service providers/“workforce” (where a product or service is provided by a third party); and advertisers (where the revenue model is advertising-based). An arrow leads to “Data give firms a competitive advantage, especially where”: data are proprietary or access is restricted; required data are less replicable (footnote a); and network effects are stronger. A plus sign indicates these conditions feed into both “Economies of scale associated with data” and “Economies of scope associated with data.” Scale points to a tendency toward increasing concentration within markets and entrenchment of market power; scope points to a tendency to conglomeration and ability to leverage market power between markets. A feedback loop states: “Greater market power may allow more data collection by firms because users have fewer alternatives,” with an arrow returning toward data as an input. A side note says effects, depending on the platform business model, can occur in consumer markets, markets for “labor,” and advertising markets. Source: WDR 2021 team. Footnote a: “Such data include observed and inferred data and data requiring frequent updating.”","limitations":"No numerical values are presented.
